memory_lessons.applicability: SIMD mappings for this kernel; timings are specific to the recorded runs and do not establish which transformation caused the difference.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline was valid at a mean of 0.39098 s, while the valid explicit eight-lane batch measured 0.17501 s. The earlier batch draft was recorded as build_failed; the successful result does not validate this outer-loop mapping.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this outer-loop SIMD candidate for correctness and full-call time, then compare it with the valid explicit-batch result under the same controller protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: The previous explicit eight-lane batch was valid and measured 0.17501 s versus the 0.39098 s baseline, but that does not isolate the benefit of its mapping. This contrasting experiment puts the SIMD dimension directly on the outer loop over independent options, with each iteration owning its local V array. Letting the compiler choose the SIMD width may avoid fixed-batch and scratch-management overhead; scalarized powf calls or spills could instead limit performance. Terminal-power generation and rollback order and arithmetic remain unchanged. The new candidate has not been measured.

retained: Apply OpenMP SIMD to the outer loop over independent options, using a per-iteration local V array instead of explicit fixed-width lane batches.
Leave each option's terminal powf expression, rollback loop order, and rollback arithmetic unchanged.
